GUARDIUM_REPORT_NAME.description: IBM Guardium canned-report name that scopes both /restAPI/online_dam_violations and /restAPI/online_classification pulls (passed verbatim as the ?reportName= query parameter on every call). Required so the executor can constrain the report-result list (Guardium routes /restAPI/online_dam_violations + /restAPI/online_classification require a reportName — the operator-configured canned report name such as 'Policy Violations' / 'Sensitive Data Classification'). Found in the Guardium console under Tools -> Report Builder (the value is visible as the report's Title column) or via GET /restAPI/online_report_list. The executor hard-validates the name shape client-side (alphanumeric + spaces + ._- up to 128 chars) so a typo or control char can't fan out into ?reportName=None calls.

GUARDIUM_MIN_SEVERITY.description: Optional client-side severity floor for Guardium violations and classification rows. Accepts info | low | medium | high | critical (plus Guardium synonyms: med -> medium, severe -> critical, major / important -> high, moderate / warning -> medium, minor -> low, informational / information -> info, and the Guardium single-letter forms H / M / L / I -> matching bucket) plus numeric-string CVSS-style input bucketed via severity_from_cvss (<4 low, <7 medium, <9 high, >=9 critical). Rows below the floor are dropped from the Faraday output after per-row severity normalisation (bucketed from the freeform Guardium 3-tier severity string enum HIGH / MED / LOW + numeric severityScore / riskScore 0-10 fallback). Defaults to info (no filtering).

name: ibm_guardium
title: IBM Guardium (Database Security)
description: IBM Guardium (DAM / classification) REST importer. Pulls Database Activity Monitoring (DAM) violations and sensitive-data classification findings from an IBM Guardium collector via GET <GUARDIUM_HOST>/restAPI/online_dam_violations?reportName=<name> and GET <GUARDIUM_HOST>/restAPI/online_classification?reportName=<name>. Each unique monitored database server (keyed by the serverHostName surfaced on the row, falling back to serverIp then a synthetic 'unknown' bucket so orphans aren't silently dropped) becomes one Faraday host (Guardium is database-server-scoped — host.os carries the database product + version label, e.g. 'Oracle 19c (Guardium monitored)', when the row surfaces it). Each DAM-violation row (one observed policy violation tied to one database server / database / user — Failed Logins, SQL Errors, Excessive Privileges, Data Leakage, Outliers, Unauthorized Access, etc.) and each classification row (one sensitive-data classification observation tied to one database server / database / table / column — PII / PCI / PHI / Custom Classifier matches) attaches as a Faraday vulnerability with the engine prefix [DATABASE-SECURITY]. Severity is bucketed from the freeform Guardium 3-tier severity string enum (HIGH / MED / LOW plus the INFO tier from VA-derived reports + Faraday-side synonyms severe / major / important / moderate / warning / minor / informational + Guardium single-letter forms H / M / L / I) with the numeric severityScore / riskScore / score 0-10 used as a CVSS-style fallback. Status mapped from status / state / violationStatus / incidentStatus (open / new / active / in_review / detected / in_progress / reopened -> open, resolved / fixed / mitigated / reviewed / closed / completed -> closed, acknowledged / accepted / deferred / waived / will_not_fix / false_positive / suppressed / dismissed / ignored -> risk-accepted; the Guardium 'acknowledged' boolean is respected as a risk-acceptance gate so triaged + signed-off violations move to risk-accepted). Pagination uses Guardium's canonical fetchSize + indexFrom cursor (1-based, PAGE_SIZE=100 per page capped at MAX_PAGES=200). Refs include Guardium-Source (dam / classification) / Guardium-Policy / Guardium-PolicyRule / Guardium-Rule / Guardium-Category / Guardium-Classification / Guardium-ClassifierPolicy / Guardium-Server / Guardium-ServerIp / Guardium-Database / Guardium-DbUser / Guardium-DbType / Guardium-Schema / Guardium-Table / Guardium-Column / Guardium-ClientIp / Guardium-SourceProgram / Guardium-SqlVerb / Guardium-OsUser / Guardium-Timestamp pivots plus inline advisory URLs. CVE list harvested via a strict CVE-\d{4}-\d+ regex from cve / cveId / cves / CVE fields plus description / policyDescription / ruleDescription / details / summary / title / violationText / remediation / recommendation token scans. Auth: Guardium REST APIs require an OAuth2 bearer access token obtained via POST <GUARDIUM_HOST>/oauth/token with the OAuth2 password grant (grant_type=password&username=<GUARDIUM_USER>&password=<GUARDIUM_PASSWORD>&client_id=<GUARDIUM_CLIENT_ID>[&client_secret=<GUARDIUM_CLIENT_SECRET>]); the access token is then carried as Authorization: Bearer <token> on every /restAPI/ call. GUARDIUM_CLIENT_ID defaults to 'guardium' (the Guardium-shipped REST client id per the public REST API guide); GUARDIUM_CLIENT_SECRET is optional (some Guardium tenants don't require it). GUARDIUM_HOST is the Guardium collector endpoint URL (http(s)://host[:port], trailing slash stripped client-side, control chars rejected on the raw value before .strip() runs so a header-injection attempt can't sneak through; regex anchored with \A/\Z not ^/$). Tags: [ibm, guardium, database-security, ibm-guardium, dam|classification].
